The Reserve Bank reported little evidence yet of AI disrupting the labour market but flagged high uncertainty about future effects. Opposition figures criticised the approach as voluntary guidance while companies such as Qantas, National Australian Bank and Canva cut thousands of jobs linked partly to AI.
items.title: Australia warns employers of AI job and wage effects

items.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit a building housing Nasser Hospital's surgical and intensive care wards in southern Gaza, killing at least five Palestinians, including reportedly a surgeon. The Hamas-run Civil Defence agency reported the death toll of 20 people injured. Israel says it targeted militants using medical infrastructure as a command center.
items.title: Israeli Strike on Gaza Hospital Kills at Least Five

items.summary: A BBC report describes how Russia's intensified attacks on Ukraine's energy grid are pushing power supplies close to critical, leaving families in Kyiv facing outages of up to 20 hours. Daryna Kulchytska, a single parent, recounts unreliable rolling blackouts that have been in place since October and are lasting longer than last winter. The article shows the damage at one large power station destroyed by a ballistic missile strike, with recovery hampered by air raids every 15-30 minutes. President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine still has enough generating capacity but struggles to deliver it home; Maxim Timchenko of DTEK warns attacks have doubled in scale and rebuilding will take until next summer.
items.title: Ukraine's Power Grid Near Collapse as Russian Strikes Intensify

items.summary: Michael Lee from the Republic of Korea came to China in 2003, and more than two decades later he now calls Quanzhou in Fujian Province his home. In Jinjiang, a county-level city under Quanzhou and one of China's leading footwear manufacturing hubs, he found a world-class supply chain, constant innovation, and the opportunity to build his own business. His next big plan is to become a true local.
items.title: ROK Entrepreneur Roots His Business in China's Shoe Capital

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands took to the streets across Spain on Wednesday for its first general strike in 14 years, protesting a housing crisis and low wages. Estimates of turnout varied widely between organisers and authorities; Madrid police counted 120,000 against an organiser's half million claim (quantity-1210-1217). More than 70 people were arrested nationwide amid clashes with riot police (quantity-86-95), while unions reported high participation in ports and industry. Unions called it a success; employers dismissed it as a failure.
items.title: Spain's First General Strike in 14 Years Draws Mass Protests

items.summary: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng Svendsen alleged that the Indian embassy in Oslo stopped her from travelling to a Congress-organised summit in Hyderabad, cancelling her visa 10 minutes before she left for the airport. She said “orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa,” suggesting political motivation tied to her May questioning of Narendra Modi and criticism of Adani and Ambani. The home ministry, external affairs ministry and embassy had not commented. About 200 international delegates attended; clearance was obtained for 316 foreign delegates.
items.title: Norwegian Journalist Alleges India Cancelled Her Visa

items.summary: Premier David Crisafulli officially reopened the New Burton Coal Mine in Queensland's Bowen Basin, employing 275 workers after receivership in 2025. Owner Argo Resources Queensland said coal royalties did not deter investment and declined to comment on previous owners' losses. CEO Richard Livingstone-Blevins planned to mine 10 million tonnes by 2028.
items.title: Queensland Reopens Coal Mine After Royalty Concerns

items.summary: The Australian government cancelled its search for a National Solar Panel Recycling Pilot administrator on 10 November, citing undisclosed changes to the industry since April’s tender release. The pilot would have engaged a supplier to collect up to 250,000 decommissioned panels from around 100 sites and recycle them safely.
items.title: Australia Cancels Solar Panel Recycling Pilot

items.summary: Cupid reported September-quarter revenue from operations of Rs 188 crore, up 122% year-on-year, with net profit reaching Rs 56 crore against Rs 24 crore a year earlier. The company raised FY27-FY29 guidance for higher revenue and profitability. Shares rose about 577% over the past year, valuing at around Rs 48,407 crore market capitalisation.
items.title: Cupid Shares Rally on Strong Q2 Profit and Raised Guidance

items.summary: Ola Electric shares rose to Rs 37 apiece, noted as only the second time in a month the stock crossed this level. The sharp 9% surge over two days added more than Rs 1,400 crore to market capitalisation, pushing it above Rs 17,150 crore. The rise follows the Finance Ministry making EVs the default and preferred choice for government staff car procurement, doubling the net dealer price ceiling to Rs 20 lakh while ICE vehicles are fixed at Rs 10 lakh.
items.title: Ola Electric Shares Rise on EV Procurement Policy

items.summary: Zhao Jiyou of the Latin America Branch of China Railway No. 10 Engineering Co., Ltd. describes infrastructure projects across three countries as part of a CGTN series with SASAC on state-owned enterprises in Asia-Pacific connectivity. The group is reinforcing a roadbed in Piura, Peru's northwestern region; it completed rehabilitation of mountain roads at an altitude of 4,500 meters and built the Santiago Apóstol Hospital in Utcubamba with UNOPS support. In Chile, its earlier railway work earned EFE awards. Zhao Jiyou says building connectivity requires both physical infrastructure and closer people-to-people ties.
items.title: China Railway Group Details Peru and Chile Infrastructure Work

items.summary: The Union government reduced India's visa categories from 13 to 9 and sub-categories from 23 to 49, per the Ministry of Home Affairs (quantity-82-83, quantity-89-91, quantity-114-116). Application-form fields were cut by roughly two-thirds. The changes aim to ease travel for tourism, medical treatment, education and business, with visas expected by end of 2026.
items.title: India Cuts Visa Categories and Simplifies Application Forms

items.summary: On Thursday, Israeli occupiers attacked the West Bank town of Atara under army protection, assaulting residents and damaging vehicles while leaving several Palestinians injured, local sources said. Clashes prompted the army to enter the town and fire tear gas canisters, stun grenades and live ammunition. Around 750,000 settlers occupy settlements across the region.
items.title: Israeli forces attack Palestinian town of Atara

items.summary: Veeraswamy, the UK’s oldest Indian restaurant on London’s Regent Street and a venue that served Churchill, Chaplin and Brando, faces closure after The Crown Estate declined to renew its lease at Victory House for renovation work. Owner Ranjit Mathrani says the business is being treated unfairly; the landlord rejects this claim. The dispute now proceeds under the Landlord and Tenant Act, with court proceedings begun on November 5 determining whether Veeraswamy can keep its lease.
items.title: Veeraswamy restaurant forced to close as Crown Estate declines lease renewal

items.summary: Former Uttarakhand Chief Minister Harish Rawat said he will not seek the chief minister’s post or any other office if Congress wins a majority in the 2027 Assembly elections, according to Press Trust of India. His stated goal is helping Congress form the state government and ousting the BJP.
items.title: Harish Rawat Rules Out CM Bid

items.summary: This morning briefing summarizes several Thursday news items. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, per Russian media (s1). Kirill Dmitriev met them at Vnukovo Airport (s2). Israel's security cabinet ordered military preparations for a possible attack on Iran, reported by KAN (s6), which warned the directives could trigger war (s7); they followed Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot's statement urging Netanyahu to refrain from operations until after Oct. 27 elections (s8-s10). Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan emphasized leaving a cleaner world for future generations at COP31 in Türkiye (s12-s14). FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem said Formula One races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will proceed as scheduled despite Middle East tensions (s17).
items.title: Morning Briefing Covers Russia Talks and Global News

items.summary: A fire swept through Parsi Parlo town in Arunachal Pradesh’s Kurung Kumey district early Thursday morning, killing at least four people including three children and a woman. Police sources said the blaze broke out around 2am and was suspected to have originated in a kitchen, though its exact cause remains under investigation. The tragedy exposed the lack of firefighting infrastructure in the remote area.
items.title: Fire Kills Four in Arunachal’s Kurung Kumey

items.summary: An article argues that India is working to revive its Vishwaguru image through a limited role in the ongoing peace talks, which are being brokered by the US. New Delhi stays off the negotiation table but focuses on protecting Indian seafarers and maintaining grain supplies for the Global South. Kanwal Sibal says these reflect two immediate concerns: the welfare of Indian seafarers and commercial shipping safety. Ambassador Anil Wadhwa notes that India's shift toward concrete proposals reflects greater diplomatic confidence, though he warns against overstating its capacity to broker a final settlement.
items.title: India's Modest Role in Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks

items.summary: The Global wildlife trade regulator CITES has lifted sanctions imposed on Laos in 2023 for failing to control criminal networks trading illegal wildlife products. Laos will now be able to trade in CITES-listed animals without special restriction, but remains under ongoing monitoring. Some conservationists called the move “premature,” arguing that Laos must do more to curb the illegal wildlife trade, which is estimated to be worth billions of dollars a year globally. In 2025, a joint Mongabay investigation with NGO GI-TOC identified 35 illegal wildlife shopping sites in Vientiane and Luang Prabang selling ivory, rhino horn, pangolin scales and other products. By July 2026 the number had grown before most shops closed by August 2026. Authorities reportedly inspected 25 shops, ordered six to close and detained 27 foreign nationals.
items.title: CITES Lifts Sanctions on Laos Amid Conservation Concerns

items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s opposition has condemned a new law enacted by President Félix Tshisekedi that opens the door to constitutional changes, accusing him of seeking to extend his power. Jean-Baptiste Kasekwa said Tshisekedi “openly declares that he wants to remain in power until someone strong enough can drive him out.” The opposition has vowed to resist any change and called for elections scheduled for 2028, though a researcher noted it is difficult to envision holding them given the security context. Former president Joseph Kabila’s armed movement threatens force against what they call tyranny.
items.title: DRC Opposition Vows Resistance to Tshisekedi Constitutional Changes

items.summary: Chief Minister V D Satheesan said ensuring quality fuel is non-negotiable and oil companies' interests cannot take priority over people's welfare. The government directed the Civil Supplies Department to intensify petrol pump inspections, with nine samples collected on November 9 from Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur districts. Results are expected within ten days, and violations will invite legal action.
items.title: Kerala CM Prioritises Consumer Fuel Quality Over Oil Firms

items.summary: Kia India will invest USD 2 billion to build a new manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh, per Gwanggu Lee, Managing Director and CEO of Kia India. The project is expected to create around 12,000 jobs and raise annual production capacity to more than 6 lakh units.
items.title: Kia India Announces USD 2 Billion Investment in Andhra Pradesh

items.summary: Crude oil prices declined as traders weighed hopes for peace in Ukraine and Iran ahead of a US-China summit, with Brent at $91.32 per barrel and WTI at $85.32 (quantity-227-233, quantity-297-303). Reports of higher OPEC production and rising US inventories added downward pressure, though Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks limited losses.
items.title: Oil Prices Fall on Ukraine-Iran Peace Hopes

items.summary: Reuters reports Nvidia’s Asian suppliers and partners in South Korea and Taiwan are reassessing plans amid speculation that Chief Executive Jensen Huang could be ousted over alleged extramarital affairs. The board met on Nov 11 to decide his future, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters. Suppliers said a less aggressive successor might slow capacity expansion and ecosystem investments. Analysts warn of possible slowdowns in Nvidia’s long-term direction, though some investors expect limited immediate impact since current chip designs are already in production. Shares of TSMC, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics moved slightly on the news.
items.title: Nvidia Supply Chain Braces for Leadership Change

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet's first Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bond sales drew combined orders of more than US$7 billion (S$9 billion) on Nov 12, per Reuters. The HK offering exceeded HK$32.5 billion; the Singapore one topped S$4 billion. Final coupon levels came in tighter than initial guidance as Alphabet expands its debt footprint for AI infrastructure.
items.title: Alphabet's Hong Kong and Singapore Bond Sales Draw Over $7 Billion in Orders

items.summary: Singapore cloud firm Megaspeed said on Thursday it cooperated with US inspections and takes export control laws extremely seriously, retaining an American law firm to census its graphics processing units. CEO James Tan Yong Pong called compliance a fundamental priority. The company faces scrutiny after reports linking Nvidia chief Jensen Huang to Alice Huang, whom authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy.
items.title: Megaspeed Defends Export Compliance Amid Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: Procurement notices show Northwestern Polytechnical University in Xi'an bought two Nvidia H200 chips from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology for 874,700 yuan (US$131,200), per a notice dated Oct 21. The management school used them; another Sep 4 notice shows the cybersecurity school purchased two more for 796,000 yuan. AFP contacted NPU schools for comment.
items.title: Chinese University Bought Nvidia Chips Amid US Controls

items.summary: Nvidia's board of directors is meeting Wednesday to decide whether to remove co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang amid uncertainty over leadership, per the Wall Street Journal. The decision follows Nvidia's November 8 announcement that it launched an independent investigation into Huang, overseen by a committee assisted by outside legal counsel. No obvious successor has been identified.
items.title: Nvidia Board Considers Removing Jensen Huang as CEO Amid Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: Spy allegations against Nvidia Corp.'s Jensen Huang are testing a yearlong trade truce between the world's top economies before their leaders meet in Shenzhen. The scandal gives Washington lawmakers ammunition to tighten semiconductor export controls as the January renewal deadline approaches, with some $500 billion in annual US-China goods and services trade at stake (quantity-2390-2402). Shares of Chinese AI firms fell on Thursday amid concerns over chip access; Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. slumped 6.8% (quantity-4079-4083) and Z.AI Co. dropped 9.1 per cent (quantity-4131-4143). Beijing's officials reject the spy narrative as a pretext for restrictions, while US diplomats warn of deepening bilateral strain.
items.title: Nvidia Spy Allegations Strain US-China Trade Truce Ahead of Xi-Trump Summit

items.summary: Nvidia’s board of directors met on Wednesday after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had two extramarital affairs, one with Alice Huang (Huang Le), suspected of spying for the Chinese government. The Wall Street Journal broke the story; The New York Times alleged a second affair with executive Kimberly Powell and cited an affectionate video from San Jose. U.S. intelligence agencies and the FBI are investigating his relationship with Alice Huang. The board is weighing replacing him, possibly promoting CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while retaining Huang as chairman. Nvidia’s stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading, shedding $1.8 trillion in market capitalization over a month. Bloomberg reports on the deliberations.
items.title: Nvidia Board Considers Replacing Jensen Huang Amid Spy and Infidelity Revelations

items.summary: Investors fear that an ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could dampen the company’s willingness to bankroll the AI boom. The board met late Wednesday amid reports of two extramarital affairs involving Huang, prompting traders to sell Nvidia shares and those of customers CoreWeave and Naver while boosting rivals Broadcom and AMD. Shares in China GPU makers Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon jumped nearly 10%. Nvidia has sunk billions into funding data centres through equity investments and commitments listed at $164.5 billion. Analysts warn the stakes extend beyond revenue to leadership vision over the next decade.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Huang's Future Amid AI-Trade Jitters

items.summary: Reports suggest Nvidia’s board is meeting late Wednesday to decide the future of Chief Executive Jensen Huang amid reports of two extramarital affairs, a shift from Sunday’s confidence in his leadership. Partners and suppliers across South Korea and Taiwan are redrawing plans accordingly. A supplier executive said capacity expansion could slow if a successor proves less aggressive.
items.title: Nvidia’s Asian supply chain braces for leadership change

items.summary: On Thursday, China accused the United States of fabricating spy narratives as a pretext for imposing a technology blockade. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said the US side should stop creating such 'spy' narratives to justify restricting chip sales. The dispute follows reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, whom US officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence.
items.title: China Accuses US of Fabricating Nvidia Espionage Claims Behind Tech Blockade

items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang is under investigation over an alleged relationship with a Chinese spy and possible disclosure of confidential intellectual property, as Nvidia reportedly considers ousting him. Shares in Nvidia fell about 8% on the news (quantity-2163-2165). Carmem Domingues said "there's not someone who is sort of prepped and ready to go next in line." She likened a fall to Lehman Brothers, while another investor noted data centres are struggling with power grids. For Nvidia itself, she sees any disruption as temporary, given its long-built ecosystem.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang probe raises AI-stability fears

items.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, three people familiar with the matter said. They fear a scandal involving Jensen Huang could prompt Washington to tighten restrictions on their remote use of advanced processors that would close a gap in U.S. export controls.
items.title: Chinese AI Firms Seek Overseas Nvidia Chip Capacity Amid U.S. Scandal Concerns

items.summary: European and Asian tech shares fell on Thursday after reports that Nvidia’s board was weighing whether to remove CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia shares dropped more than 8% in after-hours trading, while European chip stocks including ASM International (2.9%), STMicroelectronics (2.6%) and ASML (2.5%) also declined. The report came from The Wall Street Journal; Reuters said the board met late Wednesday to decide on Huang’s removal, citing a person familiar with the matter. Analysts at Quilter Cheviot noted there is no obvious successor but that Huang may stay in a reduced role.
items.title: Nvidia board weighs ousting Jensen Huang as tech shares fall

items.summary: Mark Zuckerberg said he is building an artificial intelligence agent called Muse to help him be a better father, husband and friend. During an interview on the Sources podcast, Zuckerberg described using the agent to plan weekend baking sessions with his three-year-old daughter and secure mountain-climbing permits for his older daughter. He also uses it to review MMA gym footage.
items.title: Zuckerberg Uses AI Agent for Family Duties

items.summary: Bloomberg reports Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang is in Beijing amid unproven espionage suspicions tied to Jensen Huang, per unnamed sources; China calls claims baseless. Megaspeed imported over $4.6 billion of Nvidia products since 2023 founding.
items.title: Alice Huang Beijing Report Sparks Nvidia Spy Allegations

items.summary: The New York Times reported that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang attended an event with Megaspeed founder Alice Huang, whose association with him drew attention amid allegations she was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. Between 2024 and 2026, Megaspeed acquired more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips. US and Singaporean authorities investigated her activities; Nvidia launched an independent inquiry after Jensen Huang admitted infidelity.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang under scrutiny

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is considering banning private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in more than one non-banking financial company, sources told Reuters. Holdings of 15% or less would face fewer regulatory checks. The move follows concerns that stress at a global firm could spread across its NBFC investments. Rules are still being drafted after public feedback and could be issued early next year.
items.title: RBI Considers Barring Private Equity Firms From Controlling Multiple NBFCs

items.summary: Nvidia faces mounting pressure over Jensen Huang's future as the board launches an independent investigation into allegations he was honey-trapped by a foreign intelligence operation. On November 11, The New York Times reported additional affairs before his relationship with Alice Huang, suspected to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia shares fell more than 8% in after-hours trading on that date, and Polymarket odds of Huang leaving by December 31, 2026 rose to around 88%. Names have emerged as potential successors: internal candidates Ian Buck, Colette Kress, Madison Huang, Bryan Catanzaro, Chris Malachowsky; external figures Thomas Kurian, Matt Garman, Eric Schmidt, Lip-Bu Tan and Lisa Su. Nvidia has not publicly identified a successor.
items.title: Speculation Mounts Over Nvidia CEO Succession After Probe

items.summary: Five Bank of England researchers present a structural macroeconomic model showing that the inflationary impact of an energy-price shock depends on how tight the UK labour market is. When vacancies are plentiful relative to job-seekers, workers can recoup lost real income through higher wages, broadening price pressures; the same shock runs roughly twice as inflationary in a tight market than when unemployment is high (s4). Using non-linear simulations of an open-economy New Keynesian model built on Broer et al (2025) and Chan et al (2024), they find peak wage inflation about double, with the Phillips-curve slope roughly three times steeper in tight states. They note UK vacancies were unusually high during 2022 but have loosened since, so this amplification is less pronounced now; a renewed tightening would steepen the curve again (s73). The authors state these effects are invisible to linearised models and support using structural approaches with non-linear labour markets (s75).
items.title: Bank of England model ties energy shocks to labour market tightness

items.summary: Elon Musk said it would be an honor to hire Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, in a response on X to a post urging him to recruit Huang. The statement comes as Nvidia’s board meets to consider a future without its founder. Huang faces reports of multiple extramarital affairs and is at risk of being ousted.
items.title: Musk Says Hiring Nvidia's Jensen Huang Would Be an Honor

items.summary: IBM announced the IBM Quantum Nighthawk r3, a superconducting quantum processor designed to run about 10,000 quantum operations across 520 programmable qubits. The design adds 10 chip-to-chip interconnects called l-couplers as a path toward linking two chips into a 1,040-qubit system planned for 2027. IBM noted the current production Nighthawk r2 already runs about 100,000 circuits per second and cited partner speedups of up to 19x across roughly 34 billion circuits. The article flagged that chip-to-chip links average 99% state transfer fidelity, below a 99.9% target, and that the larger system remains a plan rather than shipping hardware.
items.title: IBM Unveils Nighthawk r3 Quantum Processor Design for 2027 Scaling

items.summary: Elon Musk said on X it would be an honour to hire Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, responding to a post urging him to do so. Reports say Nvidia's board is weighing Huang's future amid allegations about his personal relationships and has launched an independent investigation led by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Nvidia shares fell more than 8 per cent in after-hours trading to USD 159.51 as the company's market value dropped over USD 450 billion since November 8.
items.title: Musk Says Hiring Nvidia's Jensen Huang Would Be An Honour Amid Leadership Crisis

items.summary: Speculation is growing over who might succeed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose future with the company remains unconfirmed as its board has not announced any decision. Bloomberg reports that Nvidia hired an external firm to identify candidates amid allegations of multiple extramarital relationships involving Huang. The New York Times reported the board met on Wednesday to discuss his position. Eight executives have entered focus, including Colette Kress and Ian Buck from Nvidia, along with leaders from Arm’s Rene Haas, AMD’s Lisa Su, Apple’s Johny Srouji, Amazon Web Services’ Matt Garman, Micron’s Sanjay Mehrotra, and Google’s Amin Vahdat. Bloomberg notes around 60 senior executives report directly to Huang, underscoring the challenge of replacement.
items.title: Nvidia Names Potential Successors Amid Jensen Huang Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: Nvidia's board is working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, according to a person familiar with the situation who asked not to be identified. The board met Wednesday to discuss his future after reports of extramarital affairs and alleged ties to China.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Temporary CEO Amid Jensen Huang Succession Crisis

items.summary: Two political gatherings in Dublin this week center on Europe's approach to artificial intelligence and defense amid rising cyber threats, according to Tech Policy Press fellow Liz Carolan. The European Political Community summit convenes leaders from EU states plus the UK and Canada under the theme 'Europe – strong, secure and connected,' with discussions likely covering AI sovereignty and fallout from Ukraine's drone supply disruption after SpaceX throttled it last month. A separate Irish-hosted meeting of 27 member state leaders will address AI governance for the first time at Leaders' level.
items.title: Dublin Summit Focuses on AI and Security

items.summary: Andrea Castillo, a Mexican university student, describes how her view of Chinese products changed through firsthand experience. She says affordable prices do not mean low quality. The article presents her account as an example of real-life encounters challenging cultural stereotypes about the origin and value of goods.
items.title: Mexican Student Reassesses Views on Chinese Goods Through Direct Experience

items.summary: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah called for dialogue between India and Pakistan, saying meaningful engagement must begin without waiting for hostilities to end. Reacting to twin terror attacks in Kulgam and Kishtwar districts that killed two SPOs and injured three CRPF personnel within two days, he said those harbouring ambitions of taking Kashmir must abandon such notions. He also urged revival of SAARC.
items.title: Farooq Abdullah Urges India-Pakistan Talks Despite Terror Attacks

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi sent Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali and Gujarati New Year greetings to Indian Overseas Congress chief Sam Pitroda, responding to a video in which the Congress leader described PM Modi as a "Gujarati friend." The warm exchange contrasted with past tensions, including remarks during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign.
items.title: Modi Sends Diwali Greetings To Sam Pitroda After Past Feud

items.summary: Bert Hofman, former World Bank country director for China, Mongolia and Korea, discusses how regional trade and investment ties are strengthening amid global shifts. The upcoming APEC meeting in Shenzhen provides a platform where economies with competing interests can build consensus. Progress may not happen all at once but can begin through practical measures like customs procedures or shared standards.
items.title: APEC Meeting in Shenzhen Focuses on Building Regional Trust Through Cooperation

items.summary: NPR host A Martinez interviewed Ukraine's former Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba about his proposals to close gaps in talks between Russia, Ukraine and Europe. Audio of the conversation was set to be released later that day.
items.title: Ukraine's ex foreign minister Kuleba on prospects for peace

items.summary: NPR's A Martinez spoke with former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, William Taylor about the ongoing peace talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine. Audio of the discussion was set to be available later that day.
items.title: Former U.S. Ambassador William Taylor Discusses Russia-Ukraine Talks

items.summary: The UK economy grew by 0.7% in the third quarter of 2026, its fastest expansion in two and a half years (quantity-23-27). The Office for National Statistics attributed growth mainly to strong services-sector activity led by IT (entity-151-181), with AI-related businesses reporting large turnover increases. Growth matched forecasts; September alone rose 0.2% (quantity-592-596) after August was revised down from 0.1% to zero, beating expectations of no growth. The services sector rose 0.9% (quantity-2321-2325), while construction fell sharply despite accounting for about 6% of activity (quantity-2524-2526). Commentators noted the UK had ceded its title as fastest-growing G7 economy to the US, and analysts offered mixed views on whether momentum would hold.
items.title: UK Economy Grows Fastest in Two and a Half Years on AI-Driven Services Surge

items.summary: The Guardian can reveal that the Argentinian government threatened Sam Moody, chief executive of Rockhopper Exploration, with criminal prosecution and imprisonment over offshore drilling at the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falkland Islands. Argentina sought an urgent suspension from Itlos, arguing Britain's agreement to drill is illegal amid a sovereignty dispute. Buenos Aires has passed domestic legislation criminalising the project and banned Navitas for 20 years. Moody said he faced personal risk preparing his tribunal statement. The UK argued Itlos lacked jurisdiction. Ellie Reeves warned suspension would have devastating consequences for islanders. A ruling is expected on 28 November.
items.title: Argentina Threatens UK Oil Firm CEO With Jail Over Falklands Drilling

items.summary: After Ohio voters ended Republicans' 15-year trifecta and elected Democrat Amy Acton governor, clean-energy advocates see new openings. Acton campaigned to reinstate efficiency measures and renewable standards, and her appointees could shape the Power Siting Board. But SB 52 still lets counties block most utility-scale solar and wind projects, and federal data shows U.S. solar farms average around 24% capacity versus a proposed 50% threshold in Senate Bill 294. Advocates hope for broader review of project impacts; critics warn the lame-duck session may undermine her plans before New Year's Eve.
items.title: Ohio's New Democratic Governor Opens Clean Energy Path Amid Legislative Uncertainty

items.summary: The San Francisco Bay Area Air District board finalized amendments last week pushing the zero-nitrogen-oxides water-heater rule into effect in 2028, a year later than planned. The measure exempts about half of expected installations to ease affordability concerns. Sam Fishman called it an enormous victory for clean air and climate. Cost remains the main barrier: switching from gas costs around $7,100 versus roughly $3,600 for another gas model. Jetson Home expects a 50-gallon unit near $4,500 next year, while RMI estimates annual savings of $360 per household. Fifteen board members voted in favor with one abstaining after repeal and delay motions failed.
items.title: Bay Area Regulators Finalize Heat-Pump Water Heater Rules

items.summary: A political-communication specialist analyses the stakes of Cabo Verde's upcoming presidential vote on 15 November 2026, arguing that the central question is whether institutions can function while preserving the separation between presidency and government. The African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde returned to power after winning May 2026 legislative elections, ending a decade led by the Movement for Democracy. Principal candidates José Maria Neves and Joana Rosa would keep both offices in one party or split them across rivals. Drawing on a 2019 study with Danielton Delgado and Susana Rogeiro Nina, the author notes that voters rarely use presidential ballots to punish incumbents, since elections often fall within the ruling party's post-electoral honeymoon period.
items.title: Cabo Verde presidential election and institutional balance

items.summary: A Vermont homeowner building an addition faced a service upgrade that could cost well over $10,000 under the standard load calculation. His electrician’s method projected around 192 amps and pushed him toward 300 or 400 amp service with underground trenching. Instead he used Section 220.87, which relies on actual peak demand from utility data; his home peaked at just under 62 amps on January 20. After adding a 25 percent buffer and new loads the traditional way, there was enough capacity without an upgrade, so contractors broke ground with no electrification cost. Experts say many panels have headroom, but acceptance rests with local inspectors.
items.title: Homeowner Avoids Costly Panel Upgrade Using Demand Data

items.summary: Chinese diplomats arrived in Lithuania for their first direct engagement since relations stalled over Vilnius’s support for Taiwan, Bloomberg reported. Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said he does not expect a major breakthrough and described the meeting as one of many stages in diplomatic talks. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius added that discussions “will reveal the substance” of each side.
items.title: Chinese Diplomats Visit Lithuania in First Bid to Restore Ties

items.summary: Sungrow has launched the PowerStack 3.0, a commercial and industrial energy storage platform built around a standardized cabinet paired with interchangeable expansion docks in what it calls “scene-in-one” architecture. The system uses laminated LFP cells and a silicon carbide power conversion system rated at up to 99.2% peak efficiency, with a stated round-trip efficiency of at least 92%. Sungrow claims an AI assistant can generate site-specific designs in 30 seconds and lift operating revenue by 12%, though these figures are manufacturer projections based on internal modeling rather than field-validated results.
items.title: Sungrow Unveils Modular C&I Storage Platform PowerStack 3.0

items.summary: A report by the think tank Climate and Community Institute examines how climate-focused Democrats won recent elections while avoiding explicit mention of the Green New Deal, according to unattributed reporting. The article cites Abdul El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate victory as an example, noting his opponent Mike Rogers framed climate policy as a tax increase threat. Patrick Bigger, research director at Climate and Community Institute, describes these candidates as green economic populists connecting climate action to utility costs. Will Lawrence will represent Michigan’s 7th District, per self-reported information. The Sunrise Movement reorganized in 2018 after its 2018 protests outside Nancy Pelosi’s office. Aru Shiney-Ajay argues the strategy must integrate climate into all policy areas.
items.title: Climate progressives win midterms without naming Green New Deal

items.summary: Researchers at Karlstad University in Sweden used light beam-induced current (LBIC) phase mapping to investigate the local electrical behavior of half-cell solar modules, finding it can detect localized defects with high spatial resolution. Unlike conventional amplitude-based LBIC, this technique measures photocurrent phase shifts using an 828 nm laser modulated at 640 Hz, revealing how changes in local series resistance affect contact quality. The team tested monocrystalline bifacial cells from Lightway Solar laminated via Sticky Solar Power's method and compared maps before and after lamination.
items.title: Researchers Show LBIC Phase Mapping Detects Solar Module Interconnection Defects

items.summary: Global AI stocks fell as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid a deepening scandal, the company said. Nvidia shares dropped 8.2% to a more than 16-month low in early trading on Nov 12, and its market value was on track to close below US$4 trillion for the first time since July 2025. The chipmaker has lost about US$550 billion in market value since an investigation into Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang began on Nov 8.
items.title: Nvidia Sell-Off Deepens After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: The Straits Times reports that corporate records show Megaspeed’s Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix pledged IT, network equipment and intellectual property to Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) under an agreement dated June 18, 2024, which remained active as at Nov 11, 2026. The link was highlighted in a May report by US short-seller Culper Research, which alleged Alibaba may have channelled funds through Apex to finance Megaspeed’s Nvidia chip purchases; ST has not independently confirmed that allegation. Apex is ultimately held by Alibaba Group Holding and registered at an address leased by Lazada Group. Megaspeed faces investigations into possible breaches of US export restrictions on advanced AI chips.
items.title: Alibaba-Megaspeed financing link traced through Singapore and Malaysia units amid Nvidia chip scrutiny

items.summary: The NVIDIA board announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer and board member. Colette Kress, current CFO, will serve as interim CEO while continuing to lead finance until a permanent successor is named. The board appointed Harvey Jones as its first-ever chair of the board.
items.title: NVIDIA Names Colette Kress Interim CEO After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: Pressure is growing in Washington for tougher controls on US semiconductor sales to China after reports that Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang advocated looser restrictions. Critics dismissed his view as profit-driven rather than national-security-focused. The Information reported the Commerce Department will soon close a loophole allowing Chinese firms access to high-end chips through data centers in third countries, while Congressional scrutiny mounts and calls grow for the commerce secretary to be fired.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Sparks Calls for Export Curbs

items.summary: A scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy may complicate upcoming US-China trade talks at the APEC summit, where Trump is slated to meet Xi Jinping. Bloomberg analyst Michael Deng told Semafor that China will know Trump “may not necessarily be able to hold any commitments he makes,” as bipartisan scrutiny of AI-chip export controls intensifies just before Democrats take control of Congress.
items.title: Nvidia Spy Scandal May Complicate US-China Trade Talks

items.summary: Jensen Huang, co-founder of Nvidia, resigned on Thursday over reports of extramarital affairs. Chief financial officer Colette Kress now leads the company while it searches for a permanent successor. Analysts cite three internal candidates: Chris Malachowsky, Ian Buck and Curtis Priem, though some experts favour an external hire such as Tim Cook or Rene Haas. Nvidia shares opened down more than 13%, wiping more than half a trillion dollars off its value. Several firms have downgraded their forecasts. Charu Chanana of Saxo noted the challenge is finding someone who can combine Jensen's technical understanding, strategic vision and relationships across the global technology industry.
items.title: Nvidia's Interim CEO Colette Kress and Potential Successors After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: Stephen Witt, author of a biography about Nvidia founder and chief executive Jensen Huang, spoke with NPR's A Martinez regarding the departure. The interview addresses his leaving from the role he has held at the company. Stephen Witt is positioned as an observer commenting on the change in leadership rather than providing details about the circumstances behind it.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation prompts biographer reaction

items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia's chief executive after reports of two affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The disclosures damaged the company's shares and raised uncertainty in markets that depend on its microchips for AI development between the US and China. Despite his rise over four years, Huang was less widely recognised than peers such as Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg. He admitted being unfaithful to his wife after revelations of the first affair.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Affair Revelations

items.summary: Nvidia's board announced Thursday that CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, citing alleged spying tied to an extramarital affair with a client U.S. intelligence officials said China recruited. Reports came from the New York Times and other outlets; NPR has not independently confirmed them. Nvidia launched its own investigation after initial reports surfaced in late October. Share prices fell sharply on Wednesday following news of a second affair involving an executive who reported to Huang. Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO, with plans for both internal and external candidates. Rep. Yvette Clarke called the White House's alleged knowledge disturbing. Nvidia still plans to report earnings Tuesday.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: An Instagram account called nswnewsroom posted a breaking claim about another Liberal MP quitting, appearing to be independent news but actually authorised by the NSW Labor state secretary. The Sydney Morning Herald prompted its authorisation label. Experts say such unbranded party accounts exploit gaps in digital election law.
items.title: NSW Labor Instagram Account Exposed as Party-Run News Page

items.summary: Nvidia's board removed CEO Jensen Huang effective immediately after reports of a second extramarital affair, appointing CFO Colette Kress as interim leader. The New York Times first reported the scandal; Megaspeed denies spying allegations and pledged cooperation with US investigators. Nvidia's market capitalization fell by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion since the first affair emerged, with shares down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday. Analysts cite strategy risks but expect limited near-term sales impact given strong chip demand.
items.title: Nvidia Reshuffles Leadership After Jensen Huang Scandal Fallout

items.summary: Kress becomes interim chief executive as Nvidia navigates Jensen Huang's departure following revelations about his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. She previously served at Cisco and joined the chipmaker in 2013, where she worked for nearly 25 years before that point. Forbes ranks her No. 32 on its 2026 list of America's richest self-made women, valuing her shares at roughly $750 million as of Wednesday's close.
items.title: Nvidia Names Kress Interim CEO After Huang's Departure

items.summary: Google is pre-selling smartglasses built with a partnership between Samsung, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker. The devices have no lenses screens; users interact through voice or the integrated camera using an AI system similar to Gemini Live. Warby Parker frames start at $395 in the US only, while Gentle Monster styles begin at $449 across the US and South Korea.
items.title: Google Debuts Gemini-Powered Smartglasses Starting at $395

items.summary: Jensen Huang is stepping down as Nvidia's president, CEO and board member with immediate effect. Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent successor, and Harvey Jones has become its first-ever board chairman. Shares fell more than 10% in premarket trading following the announcement.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Controversy and Uncertainty

items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive of Nvidia after revelations that his affairs may have compromised the company’s security, including a relationship with Alice Huang, who heads Megaspeed, alleged to smuggle chips into China. The scandal reached the White House; Trump acknowledged calling Huang about whether he knew his partner was a spy but said he believed him and thought “he’ll be in good shape.” Nvidia lost $1.8 trillion of valuation since the story broke, with shares falling about 8% after-hours on Wednesday. Major shareholders pressed the board to remove Huang before the decline spread across the sector.
items.title: Nvidia Founder Jensen Huang Steps Down Amid Espionage and Infidelity Scandal

items.summary: Moira Donegan argues that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's confession of an extramarital affair has become a matter for the entire economy and potentially national security because he is synonymous with his company. She contends that concentrated power means bad decisions by one man carry outsized consequences, especially in Silicon Valley where loyalty to Donald Trump now signals ideological alignment. The article notes Alice Huang worked at Megaspeed, under investigation over chip smuggling before the probe was halted after Nvidia's general counsel intervened. Nvidia's stocks fell when markets opened Monday and may fall further.
items.title: Columnist Frames Jensen Huang's Affair As Threat To US Economy And National Security

items.summary: Warby Parker is entering the smart glasses market with a partnership between Google and Samsung, betting demand for AI wearables will grow. The glasses connect to Google's Gemini assistant but bar facial recognition of bystanders and light up when recording video. Ray-Ban's Meta glasses still dominate at 81.3 per cent of shipments in the first half of 2026, according to Omdia. Privacy concerns persist as Norway considers a temporary ban.
items.title: Warby Parker Partners With Google and Samsung on AI Glasses Amid Privacy Concerns

Reports of affairs with two women, one linked to Chinese intelligence, intensified scrutiny and led Nvidia's board to launch an investigation into whether he was targeted by foreign operatives.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: The board of directors announced Thursday that Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer since 2013, has been named interim CEO following the resignation of cofounder and CEO Jensen Huang amid a scandal over his extramarital affair with Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect is an asset of China's Ministry of State Security. Harvey Jones, newly appointed board chair, said in a statement that Kress “has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth” and expressed full confidence in her leadership.
items.title: Nvidia Names Colette Kress Interim CEO After Jensen Huang Resigns

items.summary: Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, is resigning amid a deepening scandal involving alleged affairs with a woman US authorities suspect of spying for China and an Nvidia vice president. Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the company seeks a permanent successor; Nvidia named Harvey Jones its first board chair. Shares fell about 13.1 per cent to US$150.98 before recovering, dropping market capitalisation below US$4 trillion for the first time since July 2025. Beijing denied Alice Huang is a spy. items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Spy Scandal

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Scandal Over Alleged Affairs and Possible Ouster

Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board considers internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement. A source familiar with the matter tells WIRED that business dealings with Megaspeed likely weighed more heavily on the decision than espionage claims. Nvidia crossed $4 trillion in value and held about 90 percent of the GPU market as of September 2026.
items.title: Nvidia Board Ousts Jensen Huang as CEO Amid Spy Allegations

items.title: Nvidia Names Colette Kress Interim CEO After Jensen Huang Resignation

The article links rising incidents to improved Full Self-Driving technology and questions whether the system’s cabin camera can detect drowsiness, noting NHTSA forced a recall of over 2 million Teslas in December 2023 [quantity-6251-6267].
items.title: Police Charge Tesla Driver Asleep in Ontario as Cases Grow

items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall Sharply After CEO Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: Apollo Global Management has provided and arranged more than $15 billion of debt for SoftBank Group since 2021, people familiar with the matter said. The lending helps fuel Maysayoshi Son’s nearly $65 billion bet on OpenAI. As Apollo adopts a more defensive stance toward AI investing, its ability to continue financing one of OpenAI’s largest investors becomes a test of whether private credit can fill gaps left by traditional lenders.
items.title: Apollo’s SoftBank Lending Funds OpenAI Bet

items.summary: SBI Research revised its forecast for the Reserve Bank of India's December rate hike, now expecting just 25 basis points instead of 50 bps. The change comes despite retail inflation breaching the central bank's 6% tolerance ceiling. SBI Research cited improving rupee stability, foreign capital inflows, softer crude oil prices and easing global bond yields as drivers behind its more cautious outlook for the December MPC meeting.
items.title: SBI Research Cuts December RBI Rate-Hike Forecast to 25 Basis Points

items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.title: UP Alliance and Nvidia Board Turmoil Headline Indian Newswrap

The board appointed Colette Kress, the company's executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO until a permanent successor is named. items.title: Nvidia Names Colette Kress Interim CEO After Jensen Huang's Departure

items.summary: A two-person team integrated the SGLang serving stack into IBM's Spyre accelerator with AI coding agents, shipping roughly 1,500 lines of code. The plugin achieved about 3.6× the throughput of PyTorch reference inference and matched vLLM on Granite 3.3 8B and Gemma 4 26B A4B workloads.
items.title: Two-Engineer Team Integrates SGLang Into IBM Spyre in Under a Week

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Spy Controversy; CFO Named Interim Leader

items.summary: Eugenio Sanchez Pelayo and Gary Harper extend earlier Bank of England analysis by four years, finding the pandemic-era premium on houses over similar flats did persist. The estimated rise held through higher mortgage rates and lower transaction volumes, though they advise caution about a late 2025 increase due to possible new-build registration revisions. They also find London’s relative weakness began around 2016–17 and continued after Covid, partly explaining weak London-flat performance. Sanchez Pelayo and Harper work in the Data and Statistics Division; views are their own.
items.title: Bank of England finds pandemic house revaluation persisted

items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that Windows updates since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday cause SQL Server performance and stability issues, according to a release health dashboard update on Wednesday. The problem stems from server queries leaving connections open after completion, accumulating over time. It affects linked server queries using OLE DB providers to Oracle and PostgreSQL databases. Administrators may see rising open-connection counts even when queries have stopped. Microsoft said the issue impacts client systems running Windows 10 and Windows 11 and servers on Windows Server 202012 and later, and will be fixed with an out-of-band update over the next few days.
items.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows Updates Trigger SQL Server Problems

items.summary: The New York Fed updated its banking system vulnerability analysis using four models through 2026:Q2, reporting a $151.1 billion capital gap under the “2022 redux” scenario versus $161.3 billion previously (quantity-2316-2330). Liquidity and run vulnerabilities also rose; authors note figures remain moderate historically but elevated since 2015–2022, with a disclaimer that views are the authors’ own.
items.title: New York Fed Updates U.S. Banking System Vulnerability Analysis

items.summary: Nvidia is on track for the largest one-day market value wipeout ever, Bloomberg reported. Its market value fell below $4 trillion to under $3.8 trillion, trailing Apple and Microsoft, with its lowest level since June 2025. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid reports of two extramarital affairs; Colette Kress is interim CEO. The stock has lost about 35%, or $2 trillion, since October's record.
items.title: Nvidia Faces Record Market Value Drop After CEO Resignation

items.summary: Alphabet raised about $3.8 billion through its first Hong Kong dollar and Singapore dollar bond sales, according to Reuters. The company had set a goal of $3 billion across the two sales. It sold HK$16 billion ($2 billion) of Hong Kong dollar bonds in tranches, and S$2.28 billion ($1.78 billion) of Singapore dollar bonds, according to Bloomberg. HSBC and JPMorgan coordinated the sale, according to The Next Web. Proceeds are earmarked for general business needs, a category that could cover paying down existing borrowings, according to Bloomberg.
items.title: Alphabet Raises $3.8 Billion in Hong Kong and Singapore Bonds

items.summary: A language-model paper called “The Pain Axis” was misread as proof that models feel pain, sparking what one outlet called the dumbest AI debate yet. Author Cameron Berg condemned an ‘AI torture chamber’ project for producing gratuitous simulated suffering. The paper itself claims only that models behave as if in pain, not that they experience it. Injected models often chose harmful options, but a revised version offered alternative explanations: performative disregard or passive coping. Eryk Salvaggio argues such experiments illuminate mechanisms rather than settle questions of consciousness.
items.title: An interpretability experiment on AI distress drew a cruel debate

items.summary: The EUROPA consortium trained a ~1-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model on JUPITER, EuroHPC’s exascale supercomputer at Forschungszentrum Jülich. It raised throughput from 90 to ~1,300 tokens/sec per GPU across 384 GH200 GPUs (quantity-2050-2062). The team attributed the gains to FlexShard placement for Muon, activation-checkpoint offloading to Grace CPU, and asynchronous FSDP gathers. It reduced optimizer time from 41.7 s to 2.2 s per step (quantity-6197-6202) and cut allocator retries from 384 to zero (quantity-9731-9734). All fixes were upstreamed to PyTorch and TorchTitan for reproducibility.
items.title: EUROPA consortium scales MoE training on JUPITER

items.summary: Microsoft confirmed that November 2026 security updates fail to install on some Windows 11 devices running the October preview update, showing errors like 0x800f0989 or 0x800f0993. The issue affects a limited number of devices and should resolve automatically within 24 to 48 hours by Friday morning, with no action needed from users. Microsoft urged admins still seeing problems after 48 hours to contact support.
items.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows Security Update Install Failures

items.summary: GeForce NOW announced that Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is coming to the cloud gaming service. Developed by KING Art Games and published by Deep Silver, the real-time strategy game launches on Steam Thursday, Dec. 3, bringing large-scale battles, base building and a fight for planet Kronus. Players can command factions including Space Marines, Orks, Necrons and the Adeptus Mechanicus across more than 70 campaign missions, playable solo or in co-op mode. The title will run on supported PCs, Macs, handhelds and other devices, with downloads handled in the cloud. Wishlist is available on Steam ahead of launch.
items.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV Arrives on GeForce NOW

items.summary: On World Diabetes Day (Nov 14), the International Diabetes Federation notes that up to half of people with Type 2 diabetes have a complication by diagnosis. Andrew Choong, a vascular surgeon, says the first sign for many is a complication he believes is easiest to see and most often missed in the foot: unhealed sores, pale or cold toes, and leg pain on walking.
items.title: Diabetes early detection may begin with daily foot checks

items.summary: Ian Tan of Singapore says the country will not proceed with a UNESCO World Heritage nomination for the Padang Civic Ensemble, despite previously supporting it. He welcomed the National Heritage Board’s public explanation and argued that heritage protection should preserve historical significance while allowing the district to keep evolving economically and socially.
items.title: Singapore declines World Heritage nomination for Padang Civic Ensemble

items.summary: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland added median PCE inflation data to FRED, which tracks the underlying trend in consumer prices by ranking price changes across spending categories and selecting the middle value. This measure looks past month-to-month swings caused by volatile items such as gasoline or airfares, focusing instead on broad shifts in the distribution of price changes.
items.title: FRED Adds Cleveland Fed Median PCE Inflation Data

items.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened Thursday to immediately double tariffs on Mexico unless Mexican authorities stop what he called large migrant caravans advancing toward the southern US border. Linking the surge to Tuesday's midterm losses, Trump claimed an invasion was resuming and that huge caravans were beginning an illegal march through Mexico. The Mexican government issued no immediate statement.
items.title: Trump threatens doubled tariffs on Mexico over migrant caravans

items.summary: According to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s ‘International Migration Outlook – 2026’ report, Indians topped the list of people acquiring citizenship in advanced economies between 2020 and 2024. Around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquired OECD nationality during that period, a rise of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh five years earlier (quantity-100-109 quantity-394-397). India remained the largest source country ahead of Syria and Mexico nationals at around 5.9 lakh each (quantity-678-686). The report attributes the increase to growing Indian communities, particularly in Canada, where 2.61 lakh Indians became citizens over the period. OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann said immigrants now account for 16% of employment across the bloc and urged better access to jobs and finance.
items.title: Indians Lead OECD Citizenship Acquisitions in 2020-24

items.summary: On November 12, 2026, Rwanda and China commemorate the 55th anniversary since they established formal diplomatic relations on November 12, 1971. Emmanuel Karenzi Karake serves as Rwanda's Ambassador to China. The two countries signed 15 bilateral cooperation agreements during a historic state visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping in July 2018. In September 2024, Presidents Kagame and Xi elevated the relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership at the FOCAC Summit. Cooperation spans infrastructure, trade, technology and AI, with China supporting Rwanda's National Strategy for Transformation 2 covering 2024–2029 as it pursues upper-middle-income status by 2035.
items.title: Rwanda and China mark 55 years of diplomatic partnership

items.summary: At the Antalya summit of COP31 on November 11, 2026, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for cooperation amid record 2025 emissions. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan stressed climate finance access and responsibility of developed nations. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese urged clean energy investment and warned no one must be left behind as projected warming falls to around 2.6 degrees.
items.title: COP31 Leaders Urge Climate Action and Finance Reform

items.summary: Chinese Vice President Han Zheng attended the Antalya Leaders' Summit of COP31 in Turkey on Wednesday and delivered a national statement, presenting a four-point proposal to strengthen global climate governance. She called for full implementation of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement, accelerated green transition, disaster resilience, and deeper international cooperation, including support for developing countries. China reaffirmed its 2030 targets: raising non-fossil energy's share in electricity generation to 50% and increasing electricity's share in final energy consumption to 35%, while remaining committed to carbon peak and neutrality goals.
items.title: Chinese VP Han Zheng urges collective climate action at COP31

items.summary: Andrea Castillo, a Mexican university student, describes how her view of Chinese products changed after firsthand experience. She states that affordable prices do not mean low quality. The piece frames her account as showing how real-life encounters can challenge cultural prejudices she held since childhood.
items.title: Mexican Student Reassesses Views on Chinese Goods Through Direct Experience

items.summary: A government-commissioned review led by Alan Milburn is expected to propose barring under-25s from the health element of universal credit and personal independence payments, replacing them with a youth allowance. The interim report cited about 981,000 Neets across the UK.
items.title: Milburn review could overhaul UK welfare system for young people

items.summary: Workers for Oakland voted overwhelmingly on 22 October to authorize a strike over fears that city-deployed AI could increase surveillance and misjudge their performance, with 94.1% in favor. The vote led the city government of Oakland and the union to reach a tentative three-year agreement including protections requiring retraining or reassignment rather than firing workers displaced by AI; as a result, the planned strike was put on hold. Union leaders say automation threatens jobs across public-sector workplaces nationwide.
items.title: Oakland Workers Win AI Job Protections

items.summary: Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned as Indonesia's vice president on Thursday after court rulings disputed his overseas education credentials, which he needed to meet election requirements. Prabowo Subianto accepted the resignation with a heavy heart, praising Raka's service across 35 provinces and 303 projects. A parliamentary process may now select a replacement within 60 days.
items.title: Indonesia's Vice President Resigns Amid Eligibility and Academic Questions

items.summary: Ganquan Dao is a small island in the South China Sea surrounded by salt water, yet it holds a well of fresh water that supports life there. The item poses questions about where this water comes from and how it has made life possible on the island, without stating its source or describing the mechanism behind it.
items.title: Fresh Water on Ganquan Dao Island Explained

items.summary: The island Ganquan Dao is surrounded by salt water, yet beneath it lies fresh water. For generations the remote outpost has offered fishermen shelter in the vast South China Sea. For Xu Dehui, years caring for the island's wildlife and plants have turned this distant place into home.
items.title: Ganquan Dao Island Becomes a Fisherman's Home

items.summary: Wang Bing drives an electric lorry between Haikou and Dongfang on Hainan, covering about 500 kilometres (310 miles) each way. His truck now swaps batteries in five minutes or so instead of charging for an hour and half. He says the swap is much faster than before, that electricity costs less than oil, and his e-truck can save more than 20,000 yuan (£2,200) per month. CATL, which launched a lorry battery-swapping system through its Qiji Energy brand in 2023, plans to operate 900 stations by the end of this year and reach 2,000 by the end of 2027. Mao Shiyue notes swapping lowers upfront costs because batteries can be rented rather than bought outright. Xue Lulu cautions that drivers may still wait for off-peak times and are locked to one provider's battery type.
items.title: China's battery-swapping e-trucks may ease EV range anxiety
